newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR LOSES GROUND ON IMPORT PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR LOSES GROUND ON IMPORT PRESSURE.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed Wednesday's trading session sliding on immense import pressure, but foreign exchange dealers said the central Reserve Bank had intervened twice during the day to slow the fall.

"It's going just one way - down. There is a lot of import pressure and no receipts worth talking about, and it looks like that's they way it will be again tomorrow," one dealer said just before trade closed at 1100 GMT (1300 local time).
The Zimbabwe dollar, which started Wednesday at 10.4025/4225 against the U.S. dollar, ended the day's trade at 10.4125/4325 from Tuesday's closing rate of 10.3700/3941.
After opening at 16.2580/2980 on pound sterling, it finished at 16.2960/3320 from 16.2360/2630.
Against the rand of South Africa -- Zimbabwe's main trading partner -- the local unit closed at 2.2940/3000 versus 2.2900/2950 and at 6.8040/8190 against the German mark, down from 6.7610/7825.
